security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's TCG decoder or CHERI capability emulation gates GCTOP instruction availability on a Zytopr extension flag, when the spec now promotes GCTOP into the base CHERI extension — meaning it must be unconditionally available whenever CHERI is enabled. If QEMU raises an illegal instruction exception for GCTOP on a CHERI machine that lacks the Zytopr flag in misa/isa string, the emulation violates the spec.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: GCTOP decode guarded by Zytopr extension check instead of base CHERI capability check; trans_gctop or gen_helper_gctop wrapped in #ifdef TARGET_CHERI_ZYTOPR rather than TARGET_CHERI; isa_ext_cheri_zytopr flag used as decode gate for GCTOP in decode_opcode or cheri.decode; CHERI CSR or capability meta-operations referencing gctop_valid or has_zytopr boolean
security_spec.summary: GCTOP promoted from optional Zytopr extension into base CHERI: QEMU must decode GCTOP whenever CHERI base is enabled, else guests that rely on the always-available GCTOP (with no spec-defined software fallback) will trap and crash

findings.finding: GCTOP/Zytopr vulnerability not applicable: this upstream QEMU repository (qemu.git) does not contain any CHERI capability extension code. GCTOP, Zytopr, TARGET_CHERI, isa_ext_cheri*, and all CHERI-related symbols are absent from target/riscv/. The CHERI extension exists only in downstream forks such as github.com/CTSRD-CHERI/qemu. The described vulnerability (GCTOP decode gated on Zytopr extension flag instead of base CHERI) cannot manifest in this codebase.
findings.snippet: No GCTOP, Zytopr, or CHERI code found in target/riscv/ (0 grep matches across entire repo).

spec_citations.excerpt: {GCTOP},GCTOP,{cheri_base_ext_name},✔,✔,,,OP,1-src 1-dst,,,{GCTOP_DESC},,,,,,,,,v1 — GCTOP is listed under extension {cheri_base_ext_name} (the base CHERI extension), confirming it belongs in the base ISA, not under Zytopr.
